analysis.title: Japan: BOJ: Status Quo Maintained at October MPM, Underlying Inflation Assessed as Generally Consistent with Price Stability Target
key_insights: The BOJ held its October 29-30 meeting and kept the policy rate (overnight call rate, TONA) at 1.25% by a majority vote, as widely expected. Board member Hajime Takata dissented, proposing a hike to 1.50%.

The BOJ's growth forecast was broadly unchanged. Exports and corporate profits outlooks were revised up, and the BOJ still expects moderate growth supported by government measures to reduce household burden of higher energy prices, accommodative financial conditions, global AI-related demand and better employment and income.

The BOJ slightly lowered its FY2026 inflation forecasts and raised FY2027 forecasts slightly, citing higher crude oil prices since the summer. Core CPI (excluding fresh food) for FY2027 rose from +2.4% to +2.6%, and the new core CPI (excluding fresh food and energy) rose from +2.6% to +2.7%. The forecasts do not include the consumption tax cut on food from FY2027.

The wording on underlying inflation changed from reaching 2% 'between the second half of fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027' to 'underlying CPI inflation is at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent', citing many underlying inflation metrics at around 2%.

Risks to economic activity are still described as generally balanced. Price risks are still skewed to the upside, citing the same three risks as in September: the Middle East situation, AI-related developments and currency fluctuations. The wording that underlying CPI inflation may deviate upward above 2% was kept.

The Outlook Report added a note that many foreign central banks have shifted to raising rates since the summer and that their effect on Japan's activity and prices through global financial markets should be watched closely. GS reads this as BOJ caution about yen depreciation caused by foreign rate hikes.

The forward policy stance did not change materially from September. The BOJ adjusted the opening clause to 'given that underlying CPI inflation is at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent' and kept the language that it will continue to raise the policy rate in response to activity, prices and financial conditions.

The Outlook Report recognizes a 'shift in the phase' of policy, from watching downside price risks to watching the risk of underlying inflation deviating upward, as Governor Ueda said after the September meeting.

By unanimous vote the BOJ decided to speed up ETF sales. Sales began in January 2026 at Y330bn a year (book value, 0.05% of the ETF portfolio) and will rise to Y860bn a year (0.1% of the portfolio) from January 2027, cutting the time to finish selling from 112 years to around 43 years.

GS press conference focus points (15:30 JST): the Governor's view on the exchange rate and upside inflation risk from yen weakness, the economic impact of tighter financial conditions, the risk of underlying inflation exceeding 2%, and the Governor's latest view on the neutral rate level.
